author: nirs
body:
## Summary

Add `pull-events-stats` script for analyzing image pull performance from kubectl-gather output.

Features:
- Analyze pull events showing cluster, namespace, pod, image, size, pull time, and bandwidth
- Filter by cluster, namespace, or image name
- Sort by any field (timestamp, pull-time, size, bandwidth, etc.)
- `--summary` flag for aggregate statistics (pull count, total size, total time, weighted bandwidth)
- `--compare` flag for before/after analysis with automatic grouping by directory
- Support multiple gather directories for aggregating results across runs
- Output formats: table, CSV, markdown

## Example usage

```bash
# Show top 5 slowest pulls
pull-events-stats gather.rdr/ --top 5 --sort pull-time

# Summary statistics for multiple runs
pull-events-stats --summary out/*.gather

# Compare before/after performance
pull-events-stats --compare out.before/*.gather out.after/*.gather
Metric               | out.before         | out.after          |   Change
-------------------------------------------------------------------------
Runs                 |                 10 |                 10 |        -
Pull events          |               1197 |               1266 |    1.06x
Total size           |         154312 MiB |         187094 MiB |    1.21x
Total pull time      |          11590.1 s |           5272.4 s |    0.45x
Weighted bandwidth   |         13.3 MiB/s |         35.5 MiB/s |    2.67x
```

## Test plan

- [ ] Run `pull-events-stats` on existing gather output
- [ ] Test `--summary` with single and multiple directories
- [ ] Test `--compare` with two groups of gather directories
- [ ] Verify CSV and markdown output formats

body:
### Motivation
- Reduce false "offline" reports for hub extension modules by allowing a short recent-success grace window and by tuning the pulse timeout. 
- Remember recent successful extension test events per `extensionId` to avoid unnecessary waits when a known-good test was observed moments ago. 
- Update the success timestamp when the hub reports a `PORT_IN` pulse level 15 on the configured `hubSide` so sporadic events don't mark extensions offline.

### Description
- Increased `EXTENSION_PULSE_TIMEOUT_MS` calculation to `Math.max(3500, EXTENSION_PULSE_DURATION_MS * 10)` and added `EXTENSION_RECENT_SUCCESS_MS` to define a short recent-success window. 
- Added a `Map` named `lastExtensionTestSuccessAt` and helper function `recordExtensionTestSuccess(extensionId)` to record per-extension last-success timestamps. 
- In `checkHubExtensionLink(...)` short-circuited the check to return online immediately when a recent success timestamp exists for the `extensionId`. 
- When handling non-extension `PORT_IN` events, expanded the query to include each extension's `extensionId` and call `recordExtensionTestSuccess` for matching `hubSide` pulses with `level === 15`.

### Testing

author: copilot
body:
Adds a persistent inventory system and in-game store where users purchase power-ups using earned coins. Items include time extensions, damage mitigation, and cosmetic themes.

## Changes

**Data Model**
- Extended user schema with `inventory: { potions, shields, themes[] }` and `currentTheme`
- Auto-initializes inventory for existing users on load
- All state persists to localStorage

**Store Modal**
- 4 purchasable items: Time Potion (50¢), Shield (100¢), Space Theme (200¢), Jungle Theme (200¢)
- Purchase flow: balance validation → deduct coins → update inventory → save
- Items lock/gray out when insufficient balance
- Themes unlock permanently; consumables track quantity

**In-Game Integration**
- Potion button: click to add +15s to timer (disabled when count = 0)
- Shield auto-consumes on wrong answer, bypassing -4s penalty and shake animation
- Theme system changes visual mode icons (🍎 → ⭐ or 🍌)

**Shield Priority Logic**
```javascript
function check(val) {
    if (val !== currentAnswer) {
        // Shield check BEFORE penalty
        if (users[currentUser].inventory.shields > 0) {
            users[currentUser].inventory.shields--;
            showFeedbackMessage('Shield used!');
            return; // No penalty applied
        }
        // Normal error handling
        timeLeft -= 4;
    }
}
```

**UI/UX**
- Store button on user selection screen
- Power-up counters and controls in game HUD
- Flash animations on purchase, feedback toasts for item usage
- Error handling for blocked CDN resources (confetti library)

**i18n**
- All strings translated ES/GL for store, items, and feedback messages

## Summary

- Add `--pkg` flag to `asc builds upload` command for uploading macOS .pkg installer files
- When using `--pkg`, the platform is automatically set to `MAC_OS`
- Validate that `--ipa` and `--pkg` flags are mutually exclusive
- Require explicit `--version` and `--build-number` flags for PKG uploads (IPA files can auto-extract these from Info.plist)

## Changes

- `internal/asc/client_types.go`: Add `UTIPKG` constant for macOS installer package UTI (`com.apple.installer-package-archive`)
- `internal/cli/builds/builds_commands.go`: Add `--pkg` flag with validation logic and platform auto-detection
- `internal/cli/cmdtest/commands_test.go`: Add test cases for new validation behavior

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Upload a macOS .pkg file
asc builds upload --app "123456789" --pkg "app.pkg" --version "1.0.0" --build-number "1"

# Upload an iOS .ipa file (unchanged)
asc builds upload --app "123456789" --ipa "app.ipa"
```

## Test plan

- [x] `go build .` compiles successfully
- [x] `go test ./...` passes all tests
- [x] New validation error messages work correctly:
  - `--ipa or --pkg is required` when neither is provided
  - `--ipa and --pkg are mutually exclusive` when both are provided
  - `--pkg requires --platform MAC_OS` when conflicting platform is specified
  - `--version and --build-number required for PKG uploads` when missing

author: fderuiter
body:
⚙️ Core: Strategy Pattern for Fluid Dynamics

**🔧 The Violation:**
The `conservation.rs` module in `fluid_dynamics` relied on separate functions (`navier_stokes_time_derivative`, `euler_time_derivative`) that shared repetitive logic for convection and pressure terms. It also suffered from "Primitive Obsession" by requiring users to pass individual spatial gradients (`velocity_gradient`, `pressure_gradient`, `laplacian_velocity`) as loose arguments, which is brittle and error-prone. This violated DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) and the "Systems Core" principle of using strong types.

**🛠️ The Fix:**
1.  **Introduce `SpatialGradients` Struct:** Encapsulated all spatial derivatives into a single Parameter Object in `types.rs`. This ensures related data travels together (Cohesion).
2.  **Define `MomentumEquation` Trait:** Abstracted the calculation of flow acceleration into a trait (Strategy Pattern).
3.  **Implement Strategies:** Created `NavierStokes` (viscous) and `Euler` (inviscid) structs implementing the trait.
4.  **Refactor Legacy Functions:** Rewrote the original functions to be thin wrappers around these strategies, preserving 100% backward compatibility while using the new composable logic internally.

**📉 Debt Reduction:**
- Reduced logic duplication between flow regimes.
- Eliminated primitive obsession in momentum calculations.
- Opened the door for future solvers (e.g., Stokes Flow, Geostrophic Balance) without modifying existing code (Open/Closed Principle).

**🧪 Integrity:**
- `cargo test` passed.
- Added `test_strategy_pattern_composability` to verify dynamic dispatch and strategy correctness.
- `cargo clippy` passed.

author: copilot
body:
Educational code prototype lacks production rigor: flat namespace, no dependency locking, print-based debugging, untested AI paths blocking CI.

## Architecture

**Enforced src/ layout** to prevent import collisions and treat codebase as installable package rather than script collection:
```python
# Before: flat imports prone to namespace conflicts
from ai_cleaning_agent import run_agentic_cleaning_loop

# After: explicit namespace isolation
from src.ai_cleaning_agent import run_agentic_cleaning_loop
```

**Config decoupling** via `src/config.py` - environment variables loaded once, no hardcoded values scattered across files.

**Eliminated code duplication** - `inject_corruption` imported from single source instead of 70-line duplicate in `app.py`.

## Testing Strategy

**pytest.ini with AI markers** separates fast deterministic tests from slow LLM-dependent tests:
```python
@pytest.mark.ai
def test_agentic_cleaning_requires_openai_key():
    # Excluded from CI via `pytest -m "not ai"`
```

CI runs in ~2s (7 tests), local verification runs full suite (8 tests). Expanded coverage: 4→8 tests including `apply_plan`, `summarize_quality`, edge cases.

**Makefile standardizes operations**: `make test` (CI-safe), `make test-all` (includes AI), `make setup`, `make run`.

## Defensive Coding

**Type hints on all function signatures** - `Tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]`, `Dict[str, Any]`, `Optional[str]` throughout.

**Structured logging** replaces print statements:
```python
# Before
print(f"[AI CLEANING] Iteration {i+1} - checks_after: {checks2}")

# After  
logger.info(f"Iteration {i+1} complete - checks: {checks2}, verdict: {verdict.get('verdict')}")
```

**Error handling with context** around all external API calls (OpenAI, Gemma):
```python
try:
    resp = client.chat.completions.create(...)
except Exception as e:
    logger.error(f"Failed to propose cleaning plan: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
    raise
```

**Fixed OpenAI SDK calls** - corrected to `chat.completions.create()` with `messages` and `response_format` (was incorrectly using non-existent `responses.create()` with `input` and `text`).

## Reproducibility

**Pinned dependencies** - `duckdb==1.4.4`, `pandas==2.2.3`, etc. (was `duckdb>=1.1.0`, `openai>=1.0.0`).

**Dockerfile updated** to copy `src/` directory for Cloud Run deployment compatibility.

**.env.example** documents required environment variables (OPENAI_API_KEY, GCP configs).

author: swifthorseman
body:
## Summary

Complete the Native Memory Tracking investigation by documenting findings and root cause analysis for the 50 MB memory retention issue.

## Documentation Added

**NMT Analysis Document:** `docs/profiling/nmt-analysis-20260201.md`

Comprehensive analysis including:
- Test configuration and timeline
- Railway memory metrics analysis
- NMT breakdown by category
- Root cause identification
- Proposed solutions with trade-offs
- Recommendation

## Key Findings

**Memory retention:** 50 MB consistently retained after 30-minute load tests

**Root cause breakdown:**
1. **Code cache: +16.1 MB (32%)** — JIT-compiled native code not evicted after load
2. **Metaspace: +6.9 MB (14%)** — Class metadata from 830 loaded classes
3. **RSS overhead: ~21.6 MB (43%)** — System overhead not tracked by NMT

**Progress:**
- Before PR #173 (25 Jan): 93 MB retained
- After PR #173 (1 Feb): 50 MB retained
- **Improvement: 46% reduction**

## Recommendation

**Accept the 50 MB retention** as normal JVM behaviour:
- Code cache improves performance during load
- Retention is one-time, doesn't accumulate across tests
- 93 MB → 50 MB reduction addresses the production blocker

Alternative: Reduce code cache to 128 MB if memory is severely constrained.

## Next Steps

After merging this documentation:
1. Decide on approach (accept vs reduce code cache)
2. Disable NMT (5-10% overhead) — tracked in cleanup section of NMT guide
3. Close or update issue #166 based on decision

Related to #166

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent any code path from paying an agent or minting a completion NFT unless the job has an on‑chain completion request and a non‑empty, valid completion metadata URI.
- Ensure minted job NFTs always reference completion metadata (not the job spec) and add defensive checks to avoid empty tokenURIs.

### Description
- Enforce completion URI validation in settlement by calling `_requireValidUri(job.jobCompletionURI)` at the start of `_completeJob(uint256)` so any agent‑paid settlement requires `completionRequested == true` and a valid non‑empty `jobCompletionURI`.
- Tighten NFT minting in `_mintJobNft(Job storage job)` to always require and use `job.jobCompletionURI` (removed the fallback to `job.ipfsHash`) and to defensively refuse minting when completion metadata is missing/invalid.
- Added a test‑only helper `setCompletionRequested(uint256, bool)` to `contracts/test/TestableAGIJobManager.sol` to support negative tests that simulate missing completion requests.
- Added `test/completionSettlementInvariant.test.js` that asserts moderator/owner agent‑win and stale dispute paths revert without a completion request or with empty completion metadata, and that successful completion mints a tokenURI pointing to the completion metadata; updated `test/economicSafety.test.js` to match the tightened NFT invariant.
- Documented the new settlement invariant in `README.md` near the job lifecycle section and kept existing custom errors and interfaces unchanged.

### Testing

AGENT_WIN ...)`, `resolveStaleDispute`, and correct tokenURI minting behavior; these tests are included in the repo and should run under the existing Truffle test runner.

- Updated `restartGoogleCalendarSync` method to accept an options parameter for forced synchronization.
- Modified error handling in `SyncController` and `error.express.handler` to utilize the new forced restart functionality.
- Enhanced tests to cover scenarios for both forced and non-forced sync operations, ensuring correct behavior based on user import status.

This change improves the flexibility of the Google Calendar synchronization process, allowing for more robust handling of sync operations in various states.

> **Medium Risk**
> Changes affect Google Calendar sync control flow and can trigger additional stop/start imports under error conditions; incorrect forcing logic could cause unnecessary resyncs or load, but is scoped and covered by tests.

> **Overview**
> **Google Calendar sync restarts can now be forced.** `restartGoogleCalendarSync` accepts an options arg (`{ force?: boolean }`) and will skip restarts when the user’s import is already `completed`, unless `force` is set (still avoids interrupting an active `importing` run).

> Error paths that detect `isFullSyncRequired` (Express Google error handler, sync notification controller, and watch maintenance refresh) now trigger a **forced** restart to ensure a full resync proceeds even if metadata says import previously finished. GitHub Pages workflow was triggering on every push to main, causing multiple concurrent deployments that cancelled each other due to ~20 automated workflows pushing throughout the day.

## Changes

- **Trigger mechanism**: Changed from push-based to scheduled
  - Removed: `on: push: branches: [main]`
  - Added: `on: schedule: - cron: '20 0 * * *'`

- **Schedule**: Daily at 00:20 UTC (6:20 PM CST / 7:20 PM CDT)

- **Documentation**: Updated `GITHUB_PAGES_FIX.md` with DST clarification

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    # Runs at 00:20 UTC daily (6:20 PM CST / 7:20 PM CDT)
    - cron: '20 0 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: pages-deployment
  cancel-in-progress: false
```

Concurrency controls remain unchanged to serialize any manual deployments that may occur.

author: bardhh
body:
This PR updates the Monte Carlo simulation utility to support fully deterministic execution.

**Changes:**
- `src/cbfkit/simulation/monte_carlo.py`:
  - Added `seed` argument to `conduct_monte_carlo`.
  - Implemented logic to generate `n_trials` integer seeds using `numpy.random.Generator` (avoiding JAX array pickling issues).
  - Updated `_map_function` to accept a worker seed and generate a local JAX `PRNGKey`, injecting it into `kwargs` as `key`.
- `tests/test_simulation/test_monte_carlo_unit.py`:
  - Added new test suite to verify:
    - Legacy behavior (no seed) remains unchanged.
    - Seeded behavior correctly injects keys.
    - Different trials get different keys.
    - Repeated runs with same seed produce identical keys.

**Impact:**
Users can now run reproducible Monte Carlo experiments by passing a `seed` integer. This fixes the issue where implicit randomness (or default `PRNGKey(0)`) led to either non-reproducible or identical trials.

author: mrlynn
body:
## Problem

Forms created from templates and published weren't appearing in the application's Forms list. When users:
1. Navigate to an app's Forms page
2. Create a new form from a template  
3. Configure database and publish
4. Navigate back to Forms list

The form wouldn't appear (shows "Create Your First Form").

## Root Cause

The `QuickPublishButton` component wasn't receiving `applicationId` in its `formConfig` prop. When publishing, the API would either:
- Auto-assign a different default application
- Leave `applicationId` undefined

Since the Forms list filters by `applicationId`, the form wouldn't show up.

## Fix

Added `applicationId: propApplicationId` to the formConfig passed to `QuickPublishButton` in `FormBuilder.tsx`.

## Testing

1. Go to any application → Forms
2. Click "Create Form" or use a template
3. Configure database, publish the form
4. Navigate back to Forms list
5. Form should now appear in the list

## Related

Found during end-to-end testing of the form → workflow → email notification flow.

author: jasperblues
body:
# PR: Integrate Chat Store as Embabel's Conversation Persistence Layer                                                                              
                                                                                                                                                      
  **BLUF:** Moves conversation storage abstractions from embabel-agent into embabel-chat-store, establishing chat-store as the canonical persistence layer. Embabel-agent now depends on chat-store for conversation storage - either in-memory or Neo4j, with other backends possible in future.        
                                                                                                                                                      
  ## What Moved                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                      
  **From embabel-agent → embabel-chat-store:**                                                                                                        
  - `InMemoryConversation` - simple in-memory storage                                                                                                 
  - `InMemoryAssetTracker` - asset tracking for conversations                                                                                         
  - `MessageAuthor` interface - author identity abstraction                                                                                           
  - `ConversationFactory` / `ConversationFactoryProvider` - pluggable storage backends                                                                
                                                                                                                                                      
  **New in chat-store:**                                                                                                                              
  - `StoredConversation` - Neo4j-backed conversation with async persistence                                                                           
  - `StoredConversationFactory` - factory for persistent conversations                                                                                
  - `InMemoryConversationFactory` - factory for ephemeral conversations                                                                               
  - `EventPublishingConversation` - decorator for message lifecycle events                                                                            
  - `TitleGenerator` - auto-generate session titles from first message                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                      
  ## Storage Architecture                                                                                                                             

```                                                                                                                                                      
  ConversationFactoryProvider                                                                                                                         
      ├── InMemoryConversationFactory  → InMemoryConversation                                                                                         
      └── StoredConversationFactory    → StoredConversation (Neo4j)                                                                                   
```
                                                                                                                                                      
  Apps select storage via `ConversationStoreType.IN_MEMORY` or `ConversationStoreType.STORED`.                                                        
                                                                                                                                                      
  ## Fluent API                                                                                                                                       
                                                                                                                                                      
  Access conversation factories within action methods:                                                                                                
                                                                                                                                                      
  ```kotlin                                                                                                                                           
  val factory = context.ai().conversationFactory(ConversationStoreType.STORED)                                                                        
  val conversation = factory.create(sessionId)                                                                                                        
                                                                                                                                                      
  // Or check available types                                                                                                                         
  val types = context.ai().conversationFactoryProvider().availableTypes()      
```

body:
Original problem:
Nothing happens when I click the backpack on my paperdoll when trying to set the source/destination container in the organizer window.

From debugging it seems that the new TargetManager is dependent on GameInputSceneManager which does not fire for clicks outside of the world on left mouse up due to this check:

`
if (!UIManager.IsMouseOverWorld)
{
    return false;
}
`

Though even if this check does not break execution we still have `⁨BaseGameObject lastObj = SelectedObject.Object;⁩` setting `lastObj` to ⁨`null⁩` which is required for the TargetManager's execution.

*__Possible fix:__*
It seems that the paperdol creates new instances of the backpack control which cause the `UIManager` class's click handler's equality check to fail. This was replace with an comparison on `LocalSerial` but the effect of this change is not clear to me.

Will you please review this change as my comfort level is not high?

body:
## Problem

Xcode Cloud build #22 failed during export with:
- `Automatic signing cannot update bundle identifier "com.wordcraft.app"`
- `No profiles for 'com.wordcraft.app' were found`

## Root Cause

The App Groups entitlement (`group.com.wordcraft.app`) was added for "future-proofing" but is not actually used anywhere in the codebase. This entitlement requires additional configuration on Apple Developer Portal that Xcode Cloud's automatic signing cannot perform.

## Solution

Remove the unused App Groups entitlement from `Config/WordCraft.entitlements`. This simplifies the provisioning requirements to just iCloud/CloudKit, which is the only capability actually used by the app.

## Testing

- Build should succeed in Xcode Cloud after merge
- App functionality unchanged (App Groups was never used)

body:
`getLayerBoundaries()` was returning absolute world z-coordinates instead of relative depths from camera. This caused `getVoxelsInDepthRange()` to query incorrect positions—e.g., looking for voxels at z=-110 when the world only extends to z=-42.

## Changes

- **renderer.ts**: `getLayerBoundaries()` now returns relative depths (distance from camera) instead of absolute world coordinates
- **occlusion.test.ts**: Added 14 tests covering depth range filtering, layer-camera coordination, projection, and rendering order edge cases
- **renderer.test.ts**: Updated performance test threshold with clarifying comment for CI environments

## Before/After

```typescript
// Before: absolute world z (broken)
const baseZ = this.roundToLayerBoundary(this.camera.z, this.layerSpacing)
boundaries.push({ depth: baseZ + i * this.layerSpacing, ... })

// After: relative depth from camera (correct)

boundaries.push({ depth: relativeDepth, ... })
```
